source_text: Qua professione non est nobis arrogantiae fama metuenda; quia non ingenio meo veritatem defensam, sed imbecillitatem nostri ingenii veritatis viribus confitemur adiutam.
pass_a_gloss: By which profession a rumor of arrogance is not to be feared for us; because we confess not that truth was defended by my talent, but that the weakness of our talent was helped by the strengths of truth.
pass_b_english: We need not fear a reputation for arrogance because of this declaration. We acknowledge that truth was not defended by my ability; rather, the weakness of my ability was helped by the strength of truth.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 1.15; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
